definitions.gloss: warding off evil; exorcism; purification from bad luck
definitions.explanation: A ritual or act performed to drive away bad luck or evil spirits, typically at a shrine or temple. Commonly done during unlucky years (厄年) or after a series of misfortunes.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{厄払|やくばら}いをした。
examples.english: I had a purification ritual done at a shrine.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{厄年|やくどし}なので{厄払|やくばら}いに{行|い}く{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: This year is an unlucky year, so I plan to go for a purification ritual.

examples.japanese: {悪|わる}いことが{続|つづ}いたので、{家族|かぞく}みんなで{厄払|やくばら}いの{祈祷|きとう}を{受|う}けることにした。
examples.english: Since bad things kept happening, our whole family decided to receive a purification prayer.

notes:
A traditional Japanese practice of seeking spiritual purification, most commonly performed at Shinto shrines. It is especially common during {厄年|やくどし} (unlucky years), which are specific ages believed to bring misfortune (e.g., 25 and 42 for men, 19 and 33 for women).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {厄払|やくばら}いをする: to have a purification done
- {厄払|やくばら}いの{祈祷|きとう}: purification prayer
- {厄払|やくばら}いに{行|い}く: to go for purification

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many Japanese visit shrines at the start of the new year or around {節分|せつぶん} (early February) for {厄払|やくばら}い. The {豆|まめ}まき (bean-throwing) ceremony at {節分|せつぶん} is itself a form of {厄払|やくばら}い.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{祓|はら}い: purification ritual — broader term, not limited to bad luck
- {厄除|やくよ}け: protection against evil — focuses on prevention rather than removal
